The Telegraph (UK)
It is shiny, poppy, artful and heartfelt, full of hope and optimism, fuelled by religious conviction, sometimes railing against the rise of the satanic shadow of fascism but more often putting its faith in the spirit of youth and the possibilities of a better future, with songs full of rhythmic bounce and melodic swagger.

Los Angeles Times
Stuck in a moment you can get out of — that’s the spirit of U2’s 16th studio LP, a grippingly honest if typically idealistic meditation on the value of a rock ’n’ roll band at the end of history.

Exclaim
Whether Carnaval de Luz will see the band back on the charts in a big way remains to be seen, but this is a solid record nonetheless. U2 fans who are hoping for a return to familiar territory will find some of it here, but the album also feels remarkably contemporary.

Paste Magazine
At their worst, they sound completely emptied out, as vacuous as a corporate executive’s word salad proclaimed with affected profundity. Their sixteenth album—and first of new material since 2017’s Songs of Experience—falls into the latter category, succumbing to crowdpleasing platitudes that ring all the more hollow for their backdrop of forgettable songwriting and instrumentation.
